title: Where are we going tomorrow?
goal: Talk about plans and promises with the future suffix *-ecek*, and put together a weekend plan.
bekal: telling firm plans (*-ecek*) apart from near plans (*-yor*)
using *belki*, *kesinlikle* and *inşallah* in the right places

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Hafta sonu planı
dialogs.intro: Friday afternoon in class. Ayşe is writing something on the board; Emre is waiting for Budi at the door.

lines.speaker: Emre:
lines.id: Budi, what are you doing this weekend?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: I don't know. Maybe I'll study.

lines.speaker: Emre:
lines.text: Olmaz! Biz Kapadokya'ya gideceğiz. Sen de geleceksin.
lines.id: No way! We're going to Cappadocia. You're coming too.
lines.literal: won't-do! we Cappadocia-to will-go-we. you too will-come-you.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: Really? How will we get there?

lines.speaker: Emre:
lines.text: Gece otobüsüyle. Cuma akşam kalkacak, sabah varacağız.
lines.id: By night bus. It leaves Friday evening and we arrive in the morning.
lines.literal: night bus-its-with. Friday evening will-depart, morning will-arrive-we.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: How many days will we stay?

lines.speaker: Emre:
lines.id: Two days. We'll come back Sunday evening.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: Will we go on a balloon ride?

lines.speaker: Emre:
lines.text: Pahalı ama deneyeceğiz. Sabah beşte kalkacağız.
lines.id: It's expensive, but we'll try. We'll get up at five in the morning.
lines.literal: expensive but will-try-we. morning five-at will-get-up-we.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: At five? I won't be able to sleep!

lines.speaker: Emre:
lines.id: You'll sleep on the bus. So, are you coming?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: I'm coming! I'll buy the ticket today.

notes: **Gelecek becomes geleceğim.** Because the person ending starts with a vowel, the *k* at the end of *-ecek* softens to *ğ* — exactly the rule from unit 4. This only happens with *ben* and *biz*: *geleceğim*, *geleceğiz*; the rest keep *k*: *geleceksin*, *gelecek*, *gelecekler*.

**Firm plans take -ecek, near plans take -yor.** At the end Emre asks *geliyor musun?* — not *gelecek misin?* — because he's asking about a decision now, not a prediction. English does the same: "are you coming?" feels different from "will you come?"

**Uyuyamayacağım** stacks four things at once: sleep + can't + will + I. You don't need to build it yourself yet; the *-ama-* piece ("can't") is unpacked in unit 14. What matters now: the order is always stem first, person ending last.

**İnşallah is used far more often than you'd expect.** It goes with almost every plan — not as a religious statement, but as a way of saying "hopefully". Answering someone's plan with *inşallah* always sounds polite.

blocks.text: The future suffix has two forms, *-ecek* and *-acak*, plus a linking **y** after a stem ending in a vowel. The person endings go back to the first set — the same as with *-yor*.
Notice *gideceğim*: *gitmek* softens *t* to *d* because the suffix starts with a vowel — just like *gidiyorum*. Once you know these two verbs (*gitmek*, *etmek*), there are no more surprises.
The negative inserts *-me/-ma* as usual, then the linking *y*: *gel-me-y-eceğim*. It's a long chain, but you already know each piece on its own.

blocks.title: Two forms for the future
items: *Yarın geliyorum* and *Yarın geleceğim* are both correct. The first sounds like something already agreed; the second like an intention or a prediction.
For promises and official schedules, use *-ecek*: *Ders saat dokuzda başlayacak*. For a plan that's just been agreed, *-yor* is actually more natural: *Tamam, geliyorum*.

English

What time will you come tomorrow?

blocks.title: Cappadocia
items: Cappadocia in Central Anatolia is the best-known destination after Istanbul: valleys of soft rock, cave houses, underground churches, and hundreds of hot-air balloons rising together at six in the morning.
Istanbul to Cappadocia is about 730 km. Night buses leave around 8:00 p.m. and arrive at dawn — the cheapest option, and the most Turkish way to travel.

blocks.title: Unit 10 review
items: Cover the Turkish and rebuild these from memory: "I'd like to try this." · "What's in it?" · "Is the meat halal?" · "The bill, please." · "Enjoy your meal!"
Then turn these into "I want to ..." sentences: *gitmek*, *öğrenmek*, *çay içmek*.
